$comment: The usage delta wire (F-027-m) — the declared home of the routing key the
collector publishes a pass under, and of every field in that message.
These names cross a process boundary: network-service writes them in Go
and billing-service's metering consumer reads them in TypeScript (F-027-n).
network-service is not in the Nx workspace and cannot import shared-core, so
this fixture plus a test on each side replaces the import that does not
exist (ADR-0036, C-04, C-08). The Go half is
network-service/internal/publish/delta_contract_test.go; the TypeScript half
is shared-core/src/lib/automation/usage-delta.contract.spec.ts.
Change a value here and both sides go red until they agree.
One message is one pass over one panel. The pass is the unit that has to be
durable before a cursor moves (invariant 18), and a pass carries three
streams, not one: what we believe, what we do not, and what we could not
place. Publishing only the deltas would drop the other two on the floor,
which is the exact failure the invariant forbids. A pass wider than
maxDeltasPerMessage is split into chunks; each delta carries its own id, so
a chunk redelivered or republished is absorbed by `usage_delta_seen`.
Bytes are decimal strings, never JSON numbers: these are BIGINT columns and
a figure past 2^53 loses precision on the way through JSON.parse long
before anyone notices it is a wrong bill.
Types: uuid, uuid?, string, string?, bytes (decimal string), timestamp
(RFC3339, UTC), bool, int, enum:<PrismaEnum>. A `uuid?` is JSON null when
it is absent — the column it lands in is nullable. A `string?` is the empty
string, because the column it lands in is not.
The exchange every automation message already rides (F-079). Declared in
shared-core/src/lib/automation/bot-update.ts as AUTOMATION_EXCHANGE_DEFAULT
and overridden by AUTOMATION_EXCHANGE; repeated here because Go reads this
file and cannot read that one.
The prefix is not decoration: `automation.tick.#`, `otp.delivery.#`,
`bot.update.<slot>` and `outbox.#` are already bound on that exchange, and
a bare key is a string one domain chooses until two of them choose the
same one. A consumer binds `network.usage.#`.
`usage_delta_seen.deltaId` is the idempotency key of the whole metering
path, so it cannot be random: a redelivered message must carry the id its
first delivery carried. It is a UUIDv5 (RFC 4122 §4.3) over this namespace
and the delta's identity — panelId, remoteId, sessionId, observedAt in
RFC3339 with nanoseconds, upBytes, downBytes — joined with a single `|`.
Either side can recompute it from the message alone, which is what makes
it checkable rather than trusted.

envelope.name: version
envelope.note: This file's `version`. A consumer refuses a version it was not written against rather than guessing at a field.

envelope.name: panelId
envelope.note: `network.panel.id` — the panel the bytes were measured on. Carried from day one for F-1002, which attributes bandwidth cost to the panel's owner.

envelope.name: ownershipType
envelope.note: Who owns the panel the bytes crossed: `platform` or `tenant`. F-1002 again — the cost lands on the owner, and a consumer that had to join back to `panel` to learn it would be reading a row the collector already had.

envelope.name: tenantId
envelope.note: Set exactly when `ownershipType = tenant` (invariant 9). `traffic_raw_log.tenantId` is NOT NULL and denormalized, so the value rides rather than being joined for.

envelope.name: observedAt
envelope.note: The pass's own clock. A bulk read is one request and therefore one moment (invariant 34).

envelope.name: chunk
envelope.note: 1-based. A pass past `maxDeltasPerMessage` is split; the chunks are one pass and one moment.

envelope.name: chunks
envelope.note: How many chunks this pass became.

delta.name: configId
delta.note: `network.config.id` — the config that owns the remote client.

delta.name: remoteId
delta.note: The panel's own id for the client, as reported. Kept beside `configId` so a wrong attribution is visible in the message that made it.

delta.name: protocol
delta.note: The config's protocol. Carried from day one: per-protocol cost is what F-1002 reports on, and adding it later means a migration over a table that is already partitioned by month.

delta.name: observedAt
delta.note: The end of the interval this delta covers, as the source reported it.

delta.name: sessionId
delta.note: Set under `session` counter semantics, empty otherwise.

delta.name: afterReset
delta.note: The counter this came from had gone backward. The bytes are real; what was lost is whatever ran before the reset, and that is a fact about this delta rather than a footnote (ADR-0074).

quarantine.name: configId
quarantine.note: Nullable because attribution is one of the things that can be what failed.

unattributed.name: remoteIdentifier
unattributed.note: `unattributed_usage.remoteIdentifier` — the panel's own identifier for a client no config claims.
